# Write a polite refund request email in 30 seconds

**Hook:**
You’ve just bought something online and it’s not quite right. Instead of writing a long, frustrated message, you’ll use Cohere’s ready-made prompt to craft a clear, polite refund request in under a minute.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account (sign up at [cohere.com](https://cohere.com)).
- A device with internet and an email app.
- 2 minutes of your time.

## Step 1 — Open Cohere’s prompt library
Go to [cohere.com](https://cohere.com) and sign in. On the homepage, look for a button like **Prompt Library** or **Explore Prompts** near the top menu. Tap it.
You’ll land on a page full of ready-made prompts for different tasks.
If you don’t see “Prompt Library,” look for a search bar or a menu with words like **Templates** or **Examples**.
You’ll know it worked when you see a grid of prompts with titles like “Write a polite email” or “Draft a refund request.”

💬 Example:
Click the prompt titled **Write a polite refund request email**.

## Step 2 — Fill in the blanks
Open the refund prompt. You’ll see placeholders like **Order number**, **Product name**, and **Reason for return**.
Replace each placeholder with your real details. For example:
- Order number → **ORD-2024-0567**
- Product name → **Wireless Bluetooth Headphones**
- Reason for return → **The left earbud doesn’t charge**
If a placeholder isn’t needed, just leave it blank.
You’ll know it worked when the prompt now shows your real order number and product name instead of the placeholders.

💬 Example:
Replace:
```
Order number: [ORDER_NUMBER]
Product name: [PRODUCT_NAME]
Reason for return: [REASON]
```
with:
```
Order number: ORD-2024-0567
Product name: Wireless Bluetooth Headphones
Reason for return: The left earbud doesn’t charge
```

## Step 3 — Generate the email
Scroll to the bottom of the prompt and look for a button like **Generate** or **Run**. Tap it.
Cohere will create a draft email in a new window or panel.
If the button says **Try again** or **Regenerate**, tap it once if the first draft isn’t quite right.
You’ll know it worked when you see a full, polite email ready to copy.

💬 Example:
The draft might look like:
```
Subject: Request for refund – Order ORD-2024-0567

Dear Customer Support,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing regarding my recent purchase of Wireless Bluetooth Headphones (Order ORD-2024-0567). Unfortunately, the left earbud does not charge, which prevents me from using the product as intended.

Could you please process a refund for this item? I would be grateful for your assistance.

Thank you for your time and support.

Best regards,
Maria Chen
```

## Step 4 — Copy and send
Highlight the whole email and copy it (Ctrl+C or Cmd+C). Open your email app and start a new message to the store’s support address.
Paste the text into the email body. Add your own email address in the **To** field and a subject like **Refund request – Order ORD-2024-0567**.
If the store’s support address isn’t in the prompt, look for a “Contact us” link on their website.
You’ll know it worked when the email is ready to send with your details and the store’s address filled in.

💬 Example:
To: support@headphonestore.com.au
Subject: Refund request – Order ORD-2024-0567
Body: (paste the generated text)

## Step 5 — Send and follow up
Send the email. Keep an eye on your inbox for a reply.
If you don’t hear back within two business days, send a short follow-up email with the same subject line and a polite note like “Following up on my refund request sent on [date].”
You’ll know it worked when you receive a confirmation or update from the store.

## Common mistakes
- **Leaving placeholders in the email** → Always replace every placeholder with your real details before generating.
- **Skipping the subject line** → Add a clear subject like “Refund request – Order ORD-2024-0567” so the store can route your message quickly.
- **Sending without proof** → Attach a photo of the faulty item or a screenshot of the order confirmation if the store asks for evidence.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Next time an online order isn’t right, you’ll have a polite, ready-to-send refund request ready in under a minute.
- **For your business or work:** If you handle customer service, you can use this prompt to draft consistent, professional refund emails quickly.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one prompt, fill in the blanks, and send your first request today.

## Try it now
Open [cohere.com](https://cohere.com), find the **Prompt Library**, open the **Write a polite refund request email** prompt, fill in your order number and product name, and tap **Generate**. Copy the email and send it to the store’s support address.
